messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Online course: R Genetic Association Methods for Ecology
messages.subject_clean: Online course: R Genetic Association Methods for Ecology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-ECOLOGY members

A reminder - Bring rigorous genomic analysis into environmental and ecological data workflows. Advanced Statistical Methods for Genetic Association Studies is a 2-day seminar livestreaming September 8 and 10 with Jingjing Yang (School of Medicine, Emory University). Implement reproducible R workflows for genotype quality control, association testing, and population-structure correction in environmental genomic datasets. Use molecular QTL mapping, co-localization, Mendelian Randomization, and TWAS methods while examining model assumptions and confounding. Interpret polygenic and association signals in ways that support transparent ecological research reporting.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/advanced-statistical-methods-for-genetic
Please circulate this reminder if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] RNA-Seq Analysis (RNAA02) – Applications for Ecology - FINAL CALL!
messages.subject_clean: RNA-Seq Analysis (RNAA02) – Applications for Ecology - FINAL CALL!
messages.body_plain:
RNA-Seq Analysis (RNAA02) ? Applications for Ecology
Only 3 places left!

https://prstats.org/course/rna-seq-analysis-rnaa02/<https://prstats.org/course/rna-seq-analysis-rnaa02/?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

Delivered by Dr. Frances Turner, a bioinformatician at the University of Edinburgh with extensive experience supporting researchers across the life sciences in analysing and interpreting high-throughput sequencing data. Her work includes transcriptomics, genomics, metagenomics, data quality, reproducible bioinformatics workflows, and downstream biological interpretation.

Learn how to analyse bulk RNA-Seq data, from experimental design and raw sequencing data through quality control, alignment, gene-expression quantification, differential expression, visualisation, and functional analysis.

RNA-Seq is increasingly valuable in ecological research, allowing researchers to investigate how organisms respond at the molecular level to environmental conditions and ecological pressures. Transcriptomic approaches can reveal changes in gene expression associated with temperature, pollutants, pathogens, diet, habitat conditions, physiological stress, phenotypic plasticity, and adaptation. This course provides hands-on training in RNA-Seq analysis, with methods that can be applied across molecular ecology, conservation biology, environmental research, and evolutionary ecology.

What you'll gain

  *   A strong understanding of RNA-Seq experimental design
  *   Practical experience with raw sequencing data and quality control
  *   Skills in sequence alignment and post-alignment quality assessment
  *   Understanding of gene-expression quantification and common analytical pitfalls
  *   Practical experience performing differential expression analysis with DESeq2
  *   Skills using PCA to explore variation within RNA-Seq datasets
  *   Experience analysing complex experimental designs, covariates, and continuous environmental variables
  *   Skills in visualising differential expression using approaches including volcano and MA plots
  *   Understanding of functional analysis of differential expression using FGSEA

Course format

  *   4-day live, instructor-led online course
  *   Hands-on practical exercises throughout
  *   Real RNA-Seq analysis workflows
  *   Interactive discussions and opportunities to discuss participants' own datasets
  *   All code, datasets, and presentation materials provided
  *   All sessions recorded
  *   30 days of recording access and post-course email support

Who is this course for?

  *   Ecologists and evolutionary ecologists
  *   Molecular ecologists
  *   Conservation biologists
  *   Environmental and wildlife researchers
  *   Researchers studying responses to environmental change
  *   Researchers working with transcriptomic or high-throughput sequencing datasets
  *   PhD students and quantitative biologists

Participants should have basic experience with R, RStudio, and Linux, together with a basic understanding of transcriptomics and molecular biology.

Why take this course?

Ecologists increasingly use molecular data to understand how organisms respond to their environments and the mechanisms underlying ecological patterns. RNA-Seq provides a powerful approach for connecting environmental and ecological variation with changes in gene expression.

These methods can be applied to questions involving environmental stress, climate responses, pollution and ecotoxicology, host?pathogen interactions, phenotypic plasticity, adaptation, conservation physiology, and responses to changing habitats.

This course equips you with the practical skills needed to take RNA-Seq data from initial quality assessment through to differential expression and functional interpretation. Whether you're studying animals, plants, aquatic organisms, insects, microorganisms, or other ecological systems, you'll develop a reproducible analytical workflow that can be applied directly to your research.

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Machine Learning for Evolutionary Genomics (MLEG01) – Applications for Ecology
messages.subject_clean: Machine Learning for Evolutionary Genomics (MLEG01) – Applications for Ecology
messages.body_plain:
Machine Learning for Evolutionary Genomics (MLEG01) ? Applications for Ecology
Only 4 places left!

Machine Learning for Evolutionary Genomics (MLEG01)<https://prstats.org/course/machine-learning-for-evolutionary-genomics-mleg01/?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

Delivered by Dr. Nikolay Oskolkov, a bioinformatician, computational biologist, and data scientist with extensive experience in machine learning, deep learning, genomics, metagenomics, microbial ecology, environmental DNA, dimensionality reduction, and computational biology.

Learn how to apply machine learning and AI methods to complex ecological, genomic, and evolutionary datasetsusing R and Python.

Machine learning is becoming increasingly important in ecology as researchers work with larger and more complex biological datasets. These approaches can be used to identify ecological patterns, classify samples, explore high-dimensional data, investigate population structure, analyse environmental DNA and metagenomic datasets, and study biological responses to environmental variation. This course provides practical training in both supervised and unsupervised machine learning, with applications spanning ecology, evolutionary biology, and genomics.

What you'll gain

  *   A strong understanding of supervised and unsupervised machine learning
  *   Practical experience implementing machine-learning methods in R and Python
  *   Skills using PCA, t-SNE, and UMAP to explore high-dimensional biological datasets
  *   Experience applying machine learning to ecological and genomic data
  *   Applications to microbial ecology, metagenomics, and environmental DNA
  *   Experience with classification, prediction, and dimensionality reduction
  *   Understanding of Random Forests and artificial neural networks
  *   Introduction to deep-learning approaches for biological data
  *   Experience analysing DNA sequence data using modern computational approaches
  *   Confidence selecting and evaluating machine-learning methods for ecological research

Course format

  *   5-day live, instructor-led online course
  *   25 hours of training
  *   Hands-on practical exercises in R and Python
  *   Real-world biological datasets and examples
  *   Interactive, research-focused training
  *   All sessions recorded

Who is this course for?

  *   Ecologists and quantitative ecologists
  *   Evolutionary ecologists
  *   Molecular and microbial ecologists
  *   Researchers working with environmental DNA
  *   Researchers analysing metagenomic and microbiome datasets
  *   Conservation and population genomic researchers
  *   Bioinformaticians and computational biologists
  *   PhD students and early-career researchers interested in applying machine learning to ecological data

The course is specifically intended for ecologists as well as evolutionary biologists, bioinformaticians, computational biologists, and population geneticists.

Why take this course?

Ecological research increasingly generates datasets that are large, complex, and high-dimensional, particularly as ecological studies incorporate genomic, metagenomic, microbiome, and environmental DNA data. Machine learning provides a powerful toolkit for finding structure within these datasets, reducing dimensionality, classifying biological observations, and making predictions.

The course has particularly strong ecological applications through microbial ecology, environmental metagenomics, microbiome analysis, environmental DNA, population genomics, dimensionality reduction, and biological classification.

Whether you're investigating microbial communities, environmental DNA, population structure, genomic responses to environmental change, biodiversity patterns, or other complex biological datasets, this course provides a practical foundation for incorporating modern machine-learning approaches into ecological research.

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Online self-study course: Introduction to GAM in R
messages.subject_clean: Online self-study course: Introduction to GAM in R
messages.body_plain:
Learn how to apply generalised additive models (GAMs) and generalised 
additive mixed-effects models (GAMMs) in R to non-linear, hierarchical, 
spatial and spatio-temporal data?at your own pace and with ongoing 
support from the course instructors.

The course includes:

  * 28 on-demand videos, each approximately 45?60 minutes long.
  * Seven comprehensive modules with practical exercises and real datasets.
  * Annotated R code and downloadable course materials
  * 12 months of online access
  * Access to the course discussion board for statistical and R-related
    questions
  * Monthly live online get-togethers with instructors and other course
    participants
  * A one-hour individual online consultation to discuss your own data
    or statistical questions


The course begins with an introduction to smoothers and GAMs before 
progressing to GAMMs, model selection, validation, interactions, random 
effects, spatial models and spatio-temporal models.

You will work with Gaussian, Poisson, negative binomial, Bernoulli, 
binomial, beta, Gamma and Tweedie models.?The examples cover continuous, 
count, binary, proportional and zero-containing continuous response 
variables. This course is particularly suitable for researchers and data 
analysts working with ecological, environmental, biological, fisheries 
and other applied datasets.

Study whenever it suits you, while remaining connected to the 
instructors and a wider group of course participants through our monthly 
online meetings.

Further information and registration:

https://www.highstat.com/index.php/join-an-online-self-study-course/product/23-online-course-5-introduction-to-gam-and-gamm

https://courses.highstat.com/index.php/8-introduction-to-gam-and-gamm-using-frequentist-tools


Kind regards,

Alain Zuur

www.highstat.com

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Online course: Appraising and Improving Quantitative Research - Ecological quantitative
messages.subject_clean: Online course: Appraising and Improving Quantitative Research - Ecological quantitative
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-ECOLOGY members

Environmental evidence is stronger when analytical claims remain tied to design and data. Appraising and Improving Quantitative Research led by Centre for Applied Statistics Courses (CASC) (University College London) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Critical appraisal techniques can expose mismatches among ecological questions, study design, statistical assumptions, and reported conclusions. Participants assess bias, confounding, model diagnostics, sensitivity analyses, visual displays, and reproducible workflows. Ecologists using R can apply these checks when refining analyses of vegetation, soils, hydrology, or environmental monitoring data.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/appraising-and-improving-quantitative-re-1
The full course outline is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
